change.description: fix(chat): keep files taken during a send apart from the sent ones
change.author: Dhruv Sharma

findings.title: Restore guard in useStageAttachments now runs before the upload, not after it
findings.body: The old code awaited `restoresInFlight.get(...)` after `toWireAttachments` and right before the POST to `/attachments`. The new code awaits `restoreInFlight(...)` once, before `toWireAttachments` (line 2428). `toWireAttachments` can stream a large file from disk to the daemon, which takes a while. A restore that starts during that stream is no longer awaited, so the POST can reach a session whose worktree is not back yet. Conversely, the upload now waits for any restore that was already running, although it did not need the worktree. The new test only covers a restore that is already running when `stage` is called. If the early await is deliberate, also re-check `restoreInFlight` right before the POST (after `toWireAttachments`), so both orderings are covered.

findings.title: unsentAttachments re-reads and re-parses the stored draft on every call that does not pass a delivery
findings.body: The default parameter `delivery = draftScope && readChatSessionDraft(draftScope).composer.delivery` calls `readChatSessionDraft`, which runs `loadChatSessionDraft`: it reads storage, parses JSON and validates it (chat-drafts.ts:929). That now happens on each render in the `optimisticSend || nextDraftHasChanged` branch at line 936 whenever `durableDelivery` is undefined, because passing `undefined` triggers the default. It also happens once per file inside the read loop at useFileAttachments.ts:477 and again at line 515. When a delivery is already in memory (`durableDelivery`), pass it rather than falling back to storage. In the per-file loop, read the delivery once per batch.

findings.title: Explanatory comment removed with no code change beside it
findings.body: The deleted two-line comment explained why `onStageAttachments` is gated on `sessionIsActive(session) || commands.resumingAgent`. That gate is unchanged, and the diff leaves no replacement. The comment is still accurate and is the only explanation of the gate. It is also unrelated to this fix. Restore it.

findings.title: New `unsentAttachments` option has no doc comment
findings.body: The neighbouring options (`maxAttachmentBytes` and others) carry doc comments. This one changes what counts toward `MAX_ATTACHMENTS`, but it is undocumented. The option does not filter what is stored, and it applies in only two places: the count check and the `accepted` list. State in the option's doc comment that the hook keeps sent files in `attachments` until `dropSent` removes them.

contracts.action: Files taken during a send are kept apart from the files of the message being sent (filtered by id against the in-flight delivery) and dropped from the hook once the send is accepted or parked
contracts.equivalent_path: The old persistAttachments filtered the persisted descriptors by the delivery's attachment ids (read from storage). The strip filtered by durableDelivery ids.
contracts.before_after: Before: only persistence and the strip excluded sent ids, so the hook still counted them toward the 8-file cap and kept them after acceptance. After: `unsentAttachments` is shared by persistence, the strip, the cap check, the empty-box restore and the held-Enter check. `dropSent` runs from `acceptAndClearDurableDelivery` (line 1252) and from the park effect (line 1415), and also updates the shared entry.
contracts.visible_effect: The next message's files no longer count against the sent message's limit. They are not re-sent after a hidden/remounted chat. A file-only next message is held and sent right after the first send settles, and the Remove button works during an optimistic send.
contracts.failure_mode: If the storage read in `unsentAttachments` fails or returns an empty draft, the filter is a no-op and sent files reappear in the strip or in persisted descriptors. The code never surfaces that failure.

contracts.action: Restores are registered in a module-level map by the useRestoreSession wrapper, and useStageAttachments waits on that map
contracts.equivalent_path: The old `restoresInFlight` map in useConversation.ts was filled only by the send-path restore and awaited after `toWireAttachments`.
contracts.before_after: Before: only the restore started by a send was visible to staging. After: every restore started through the hook, including a Restore button elsewhere, is registered. The entry is removed in `.finally` only if it is still the same promise. Staging awaits it before `toWireAttachments`, and `assertRestored` turns a non-success result into SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED. SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE counts as already live.
contracts.visible_effect: A file added while a restore started elsewhere is running now waits for it. A failed restore shows its reason in the composer alert (ChatComposer.tsx:2518).
contracts.failure_mode: A restore that starts during the upload is not awaited (see finding at useConversation.ts:2428). The map is module-level, so a restore started in one window is not seen by staging in another.

summary:
I found no blocker or defect that is wrong today. The fix separates the files taken during a send from the sent ones: one shared `unsentAttachments` filter, a new `dropSent` in the hook, and a restore registry that staging now waits on. It holds up against the surrounding code, and the new tests cover the remount, hidden-chat, file-limit, file-only Enter, refused-send and restore-failure cases. I left four notes at "consider", none of them blocking:
- **Restore guard order:** `useStageAttachments` now waits for a running restore before the upload instead of after it, so a restore that starts during a long upload is not awaited.
- **Storage reads:** `unsentAttachments` re-reads and re-parses the stored draft on every call that passes no delivery, including once per file in the read loop.
- **Comment removal:** a still-accurate comment in `SessionChatSurface.tsx` was removed without a reason.
- **Undocumented option:** the new `unsentAttachments` option has no doc comment.
